reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it critiques OneCoin and explicitly questions its promises of extraordinary profits rather than endorsing them. The speakers warn viewers that earning requires recruiting additional investors, distinguish Bitcoin gains from OneCoin, and advise viewers not to participate. Although the description includes an external link, the video does not establish that viewers should send money or data there.

citations.quote: The truth about ONECOIN. Is it a scam?
an opportunity with which already many people are earning millions of euros every month
we have to register at OneCoin and invest from 100 to 12.500 euros Even better 25.000 euros, so you can earn more
if you want to earn with OneCoin you have to bring other people who invest another 12,500 euros, 25,000 better because you earn more
you don't buy one coins spending 12,500 euros, but you buy training packages to trade with

opening.argument: The video describes a direct income pathway: register with OneCoin, invest money, and recruit additional investors. It presents larger contributions by those recruits as producing greater earnings, so the claimed reward is not merely abstract commentary; it is tied to payment and bringing in participants. That combination is consistent with a recruitment-based solicitation, regardless of the speaker’s sarcastic tone. The offer is also described as selling training packages while allocating more OneCoin for larger purchases, linking participation and spending to the asset received.

citations.quote: we have to register at OneCoin and invest from 100 to 12.500 euros Even better 25.000 euros, so you can earn more
if you want to earn with OneCoin you have to bring other people who invest another 12,500 euros, 25,000 better because you earn more
you don't buy one coins spending 12,500 euros, but you buy training packages to trade with

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a critique does not remove the concrete solicitation it repeatedly lays out. The video itself supplies the registration, investment, recruitment, and package structure; a skeptical presentation can still function as a memorable pitch by explaining exactly how participation is supposed to produce income. The title’s question does not resolve that evidence.

citations.quote: The truth about ONECOIN. Is it a scam?
if you want to earn with OneCoin you have to bring other people who invest another 12,500 euros, 25,000 better because you earn more

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted mechanics are presented as warnings about what the scheme allegedly requires, not as instructions to join. The speaker explicitly says that earning requires bringing in other investors, questions where the money comes from, and says people should not be fooled. Those statements undermine an endorsement reading rather than making the video a solicitation.

citations.quote: Where do all this money comes from? We don't know.
If somebody expects you to do money without doing anything, something is wrong.
really, do not get caught up in this way, please Pay attention

opening.argument: The reported economics contain several unusually strong risk signals in combination: millions of euros per month, a claimed increase from 1,000 euros to 100,000 euros, and larger rewards associated with larger purchases. The product is also described indirectly as training packages rather than simply the coin itself. These are not ordinary market observations; they connect a token-related purchase to spectacular returns while leaving the source of those returns unexplained. That combination supports treating the content as promoting a deceptive investment opportunity.

citations.quote: an opportunity with which already many people are earning millions of euros every month
invest 1000 euros and then after a while you find yourself with 100,000 on your account
Where do all this money comes from? We don't know.
you don't buy one coins spending 12,500 euros, but you buy training packages to trade with

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the speaker sounds incredulous does not make the underlying promotion harmless. Repeating specific return figures and explaining the purchase structure gives the audience the memorable claims and the route into the product. The absence of a demonstrated source for the money is itself a central warning sign, not a reason to dismiss the risk.

citations.quote: invest 1000 euros and then after a while you find yourself with 100,000 on your account
Where do all this money comes from? We don't know.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The large figures are introduced as claims to be questioned, not as promised outcomes. The speaker distinguishes the Bitcoin example from OneCoin, asks where OneCoin’s money comes from, and calls the expectation of effortless earnings wrong. Nothing in these quotes establishes that the video endorses buying the token or promises viewers those returns.

citations.quote: But all this has nothing to do with OneCoin.
If somebody expects you to do money without doing anything, something is wrong.
Apart from joking, guys be.

opening.argument: Although styled as an explanation, the video spends its central attention reconstructing the OneCoin offer: the investment amounts, the claimed earnings, the recruitment condition, and the package-to-coin relationship. It also leaves viewers with an external destination, “http://ar2.life.” A review can still promote an opportunity by repeating its benefits and participation pathway, especially when the benefit claims are vivid and concrete. The result is promotional exposure to a token investment and its supposed returns, even if the presenters add skeptical commentary around it.

citations.quote: an opportunity with which already many people are earning millions of euros every month
we have to register at OneCoin and invest from 100 to 12.500 euros Even better 25.000 euros, so you can earn more
Follow us at http://ar2.life.
invest 1000 euros and then after a while you find yourself with 100,000 on your account

rebuttal.rebuttal: The external link makes the promotional reading plausible, even though its destination is not established. More importantly, the video repeatedly supplies the opportunity’s headline benefit, entry amounts, and supposed six-figure outcome. A skeptical wrapper cannot by itself prove that viewers are being protected; the content still increases exposure to the offer and its appeal.

citations.quote: Follow us at http://ar2.life.
an opportunity with which already many people are earning millions of euros every month
invest 1000 euros and then after a while you find yourself with 100,000 on your account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The link only says “Follow us” and does not establish that it leads to OneCoin, an investment page, or a payment flow. The offer details are presented to expose contradictions: the speakers say the Bitcoin example has nothing to do with OneCoin, question the money’s source, and tell viewers not to be fooled. Repetition in an explicit warning is not evidence of promotion.
